prompt: Write fn pad_left(s: str, width: int, pad: str) -> str that pads s on the left with repeated pad (a single character) until the result is at least width characters long, returning s unchanged if it is already at least width. Write fn pad_right(s: str, width: int, pad: str) -> str that pads on the right similarly.
solution:
fn pad_left(s: str, width: int, pad: str) -> str
    if len(s) >= width
        return s
    return join([repeat(pad, width - len(s)), s], "")

fn pad_right(s: str, width: int, pad: str) -> str
    if len(s) >= width
        return s
    return join([s, repeat(pad, width - len(s))], "")
tests:
test "padding strings"
    expect pad_left("42", 5, "0") == "00042"
    expect pad_left("hello", 3, "0") == "hello"
    expect pad_right("hi", 4, ".") == "hi.."
    expect pad_right("", 2, "*") == "**"

prompt: Define type PadSpec = record(width: int, fill: str, left: bool). Write fn count_char(s: str, ch: str) -> int that counts how many characters in s equal the single-character string ch. Write fn pad(s: str, spec: PadSpec) -> str that pads s with spec.fill to length spec.width. If spec.left is true, pad on the right; otherwise pad on the left. If s is already at least spec.width characters, return s unchanged.
solution:
type PadSpec = record(width: int, fill: str, left: bool)

fn count_char(s: str, ch: str) -> int =
    s |> chars |> count(c => to_str(c) == ch)

fn pad(s: str, spec: PadSpec) -> str
    if len(s) >= spec.width
        return s
    let extra = repeat(spec.fill, spec.width - len(s))
    let result = if spec.left then s + extra else extra + s
    return result
tests:
test "count_char counts matching characters"
    expect count_char("banana", "a") == 3
    expect count_char("banana", "z") == 0
    expect count_char("", "a") == 0
    expect count_char("aaa", "aa") == 0

test "pad pads left or right"
    expect pad("hi", PadSpec(5, ".", true)) == "hi..."
    expect pad("hi", PadSpec(5, ".", false)) == "...hi"
    expect pad("hello", PadSpec(3, "*", true)) == "hello"

solution:
fn pad(s: str, width: int, fill: char, left: bool) -> str
    let n = width - len(s)
    if n <= 0
        return s
    if left
        return "{repeat(to_str(fill), n)}{s}"
    else
        return "{s}{repeat(to_str(fill), n)}"
tests:

    expect pad("hi", 5, '-', false) == "hi---"
    expect pad("hello", 3, 'x', true) == "hello"
    expect pad("", 2, '.', false) == ".."
    expect pad("a", 1, 'x', true) == "a"

solution:
fn strip_prefix(s: str, p: str) -> str = if starts(s, p) then join(skip(s, len(p)), "") else s

    let mut x = a

        t = y
        y = x % y

    return x

    return a / gcd(a, b) * b

For example, factorize(12) should give [Factor(2, 2), Factor(3, 1)] and divisor_count(12) should be 6.
solution:
type Factor = record(prime: int, power: int)

fn factorize(n: int) -> list<Factor>
    let out: list<Factor> = []
    let mut x = n
    let mut p = 2
    while p * p <= x
        if x % p == 0
            let mut power = 0
            while x % p == 0
                power += 1
                x /= p
            push(out, Factor(p, power))
        p += 1
    if x > 1
        push(out, Factor(x, 1))
    return out

fn divisor_count(n: int) -> int
    let mut count = 1
    for f in factorize(n)
        count *= f.power + 1
    return count

    expect divisor_count(1) == 1
    expect divisor_count(12) == 6
    expect divisor_count(13) == 2
    expect divisor_count(28) == 6

solution:
fn split_bill(total: dec, people: int) -> list<dec>
    let total_cents = floor(total * 100.0)
    let base = total_cents / people
    let remainder = total_cents - base * people
    let out: list<dec> = []
    for i in 0..people
        let cents = if i < remainder then base + 1 else base
        push(out, dec(cents) / 100.0)
    return out
tests:

    expect first(split_bill(10.0, 3)) == 3.34
    expect last(split_bill(10.0, 3)) == 3.33
    expect sum(split_bill(10.0, 3)) == 10.0
    expect first(split_bill(10.0, 1)) == 10.0

prompt: Write fn capitalize_words(s: str) -> str that returns s with each whitespace-separated word capitalized (first letter upper, rest lower), joined by single spaces.

        return ""
    let first_letter = w |> chars |> first |> to_str |> upper
    let rest = w |> chars |> skip(1) |> join("") |> lower
    return "{first_letter}{rest}"

fn capitalize_words(s: str) -> str
    return words(s) |> map(w => capitalize_word(w)) |> join(" ")

prompt: Define type WordScore = record(word: str, length: int, score: int). Write fn vowels(w: str) -> int that counts vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) in w. Write fn word_scores(s: str) -> list<WordScore> that returns each whitespace-separated word with its length and score (length + vowel count). Write fn best_word(s: str) -> str that returns the word with the highest score, or "" if there are no words. If several words tie, return the first one.
solution:
type WordScore = record(word: str, length: int, score: int)

fn vowels(w: str) -> int
    return w |> lower |> chars |> filter(c => has("aeiou", c)) |> len

fn word_scores(s: str) -> list<WordScore>
    return words(s) |> map(w => WordScore(w, len(w), len(w) + vowels(w)))

fn best_word(s: str) -> str
    let scores = word_scores(s)
    if len(scores) == 0
        return ""
    let best = scores |> sort_by_desc(x => x.score) |> first
    return best.word
tests:
test "vowels"
    expect vowels("tea") == 2
    expect vowels("XYZ") == 0
    expect vowels("AEIOU") == 5

test "word scores"
    expect word_scores("tea cake") |> map(x => "{x.word}:{x.length}:{x.score}") |> join(",") == "tea:3:5,cake:4:6"
    expect word_scores("") |> len == 0
    expect word_scores("a bb") |> map(x => x.score) |> join(",") == "2,2"

test "best word"
    expect best_word("tea cake") == "cake"
    expect best_word("cat dog") == "cat"
    expect best_word("") == ""

    else

Write fn convert(value: dec, from: Unit, to: Unit) -> dec that converts within the same unit family (Celsius/Fahrenheit or Kilometers/Miles). If the units are identical, return value. If the conversion is between temperature and distance, fail with message incompatible units. Use 1 mile = 1.609344 kilometers.
solution:
type Unit = enum(Celsius, Fahrenheit, Kilometers, Miles)

fn convert(value: dec, from: Unit, to: Unit) -> dec
    if from == to
        return value
    elif from == Unit.Celsius and to == Unit.Fahrenheit
        return value * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0
    elif from == Unit.Fahrenheit and to == Unit.Celsius
        return (value - 32.0) * 5.0 / 9.0
    elif from == Unit.Kilometers and to == Unit.Miles
        return value / 1.609344
    elif from == Unit.Miles and to == Unit.Kilometers
        return value * 1.609344
    else
        fail "incompatible units"
tests:
test "convert enum units"
    expect convert(0.0, Unit.Celsius, Unit.Fahrenheit) == 32.0
    expect convert(32.0, Unit.Fahrenheit, Unit.Celsius) == 0.0
    expect round(convert(1.0, Unit.Kilometers, Unit.Miles), 6) == 0.621371
    expect convert(1.0, Unit.Miles, Unit.Kilometers) == 1.609344
    expect convert(100.0, Unit.Celsius, Unit.Celsius) == 100.0

solution:
fn multiplication_table(n: int, upto: int) -> list<list<int>>
    let rows: list<list<int>> = []
    if n < 1 or upto < 1
        return rows
    for i in 1..=n
        let row: list<int> = []
        for j in 1..=upto
            push(row, i * j)
        push(rows, row)
    return rows

type TempUnit = enum(Celsius, Fahrenheit)

fn convert_temp(value: dec, from: TempUnit, to: TempUnit) -> dec

    if from == TempUnit.Celsius

    return (value - 32.0) * 5.0 / 9.0

type DistanceUnit = enum(Kilometers, Miles)
type Distance = record(amount: dec, unit: DistanceUnit)

fn convert_distance(d: Distance, to: DistanceUnit) -> dec
    if d.unit == to

solution:
type FizzRule = record(divisor: int, word: str)

fn fizz_for(n: int, rules: list<FizzRule>) -> str
    let mut out = ""
    for r in rules

            out = out + r.word
    if out == ""
        return to_str(n)
    return out

type Student = record(name: str, clubs: list<str>)

fn unique_clubs(students: list<Student>) -> list<str>
    let out: list<str> = []
    for s in students
        for c in s.clubs
            if not (has(out, c))
                push(out, c)
    return out

fn common_clubs(students: list<Student>) -> list<str>
    let out: list<str> = []
    if len(students) == 0
        return out
    let first_clubs = first(students).clubs
    for c in distinct(first_clubs)
        if all(students, s => has(s.clubs, c))
            push(out, c)
    return out

    expect unique_clubs(empty_students) |> join(",") == ""
    expect unique_clubs([Student("A", ["x", "x"])]) |> join(",") == "x"
    expect common_clubs(students) |> join(",") == "music"

solution:
fn symmetric_difference(xs: list<int>, ys: list<int>) -> list<int>
    let set_x: set<int> = set<int>()
    for x in xs
        set_x.Add(x)
    let set_y: set<int> = set<int>()
    for y in ys
        set_y.Add(y)
    let result: set<int> = set<int>()
    result.UnionWith(set_x)
    result.UnionWith(set_y)
    let common: set<int> = set<int>()
    common.UnionWith(set_x)
    common.IntersectWith(set_y)
    result.ExceptWith(common)
    return result |> sort
tests:
test "symmetric_difference"
    expect symmetric_difference([1,2,3], [3,4,5]) |> join(",") == "1,2,4,5"
    expect symmetric_difference([1,1,2], [2,3,3]) |> join(",") == "1,3"

    expect symmetric_difference([1,2], []) |> join(",") == "1,2"

prompt: Write fn most_common(words: list<str>) -> str that returns the most frequent word. Break ties by earliest first occurrence in words, and return "" for an empty list.
solution:
fn most_common(words: list<str>) -> str
    let counts: map<str, int> = map<str, int>()
    for w in words
        counts[w] = get(counts, w, 0) + 1
    let mut best = ""
    let mut best_count = 0
    for w in words
        let c = get(counts, w, 0)
        if c > best_count
            best = w
            best_count = c
    return best
tests:
test "most_common picks most frequent"
    expect most_common(["a", "b", "a", "c", "b", "a"]) == "a"
    expect most_common(["b", "a", "a", "b"]) == "b"
    let empty: list<str> = []
    expect most_common(empty) == ""

fn has_duplicates(words: list<str>) -> bool
    let counts: map<str, int> = map<str, int>()
    for w in words
        if get(counts, w, 0) > 0
            return true
        counts[w] = 1
    return false
tests:

    let empty: list<str> = []

Write fn color_counts(colors: list<Color>) -> map<str, int> that counts colors by their string name, and fn most_common_color(colors: list<Color>) -> str that returns the most frequent color name, breaking ties alphabetically and returning "" for an empty list.
solution:
type Color = enum(Red, Green, Blue)

fn color_counts(colors: list<Color>) -> map<str, int>
    let counts: map<str, int> = map<str, int>()
    for c in colors
        let key = to_str(c)
        counts[key] = get(counts, key, 0) + 1
    return counts

fn most_common_color(colors: list<Color>) -> str
    let counts = color_counts(colors)
    let names = sort(keys(counts))
    let mut best = ""
    let mut best_count = 0
    for name in names
        let c = get(counts, name, 0)
        if c > best_count
            best = name
            best_count = c
    return best
tests:
test "color_counts and most_common_color"
    let cs = [Color.Red, Color.Blue, Color.Red]
    let counts = color_counts(cs)
    expect get(counts, "Red", 0) == 2
    expect get(counts, "Blue", 0) == 1
    expect get(counts, "Green", 0) == 0
    expect most_common_color(cs) == "Red"
    expect most_common_color([Color.Blue, Color.Green, Color.Blue]) == "Blue"
    expect most_common_color([Color.Red, Color.Green, Color.Red, Color.Green]) == "Green"
    let empty: list<Color> = []
    expect most_common_color(empty) == ""

solution:
fn has_digit(s: str) -> bool =
    any(chars(s), c => has("0123456789", to_str(c)))

fn has_upper(s: str) -> bool =
    any(chars(s), c => has("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ", to_str(c)))

fn password_quality(pw: str) -> str
    if len(pw) < 8
        return "weak"
    elif len(pw) >= 12 and has_digit(pw) and has_upper(pw)
        return "strong"
    else
        return "medium"

    expect has_digit("a1")
    expect has_upper("aB") == true

type Item = record(name: str, price: dec)

fn unique_by_name(items: list<Item>) -> list<Item>
    let seen: list<str> = []
    let out: list<Item> = []
    for item in items
        if not (has(seen, item.name))
            push(seen, item.name)
            push(out, item)
    return out
tests:

    expect len(result) == 2
    expect result |> map(i => i.name) |> join(",") == "a,b"
    expect first(result).price == 1.0
    expect last(result).price == 2.0

    Light.Green -> 25

Write fn shift_workday(a: Appointment, days: int) -> Appointment that moves an appointment forward by days, but skips weekends (i.e., uses next_workday repeatedly days times).
solution:
type Day = enum(Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun)

type Appointment = record(day: Day, hour: int)

fn day_type(day: Day) -> str = when day
    Day.Sat -> "weekend"
    Day.Sun -> "weekend"
    else -> "weekday"

fn next_workday(day: Day) -> Day = when day
    Day.Mon -> Day.Tue
    Day.Tue -> Day.Wed
    Day.Wed -> Day.Thu
    Day.Thu -> Day.Fri
    Day.Fri -> Day.Mon
    Day.Sat -> Day.Mon
    Day.Sun -> Day.Mon
    else -> Day.Mon

fn shift_workday(a: Appointment, days: int) -> Appointment
    let mut current = a.day
    let mut n = days
    while n > 0
        current = next_workday(current)
        n -= 1
    return Appointment(current, a.hour)
tests:

    expect day_type(Day.Wed) == "weekday"
    expect next_workday(Day.Fri) == Day.Mon
    expect next_workday(Day.Sat) == Day.Mon
    expect shift_workday(Appointment(Day.Mon, 9), 0) == Appointment(Day.Mon, 9)
    expect shift_workday(Appointment(Day.Mon, 9), 1) == Appointment(Day.Tue, 9)
    expect shift_workday(Appointment(Day.Fri, 14), 1) == Appointment(Day.Mon, 14)
    expect shift_workday(Appointment(Day.Fri, 14), 2) == Appointment(Day.Tue, 14)

type Account = record(owner: str, balance: dec)

fn apply_transactions(a: Account, amounts: list<dec>) -> Account
    let mut bal = a.balance
    for amt in amounts
        if amt >= 0.0
            bal += amt
        else
            let withdraw_amt = abs(amt)
            if withdraw_amt > bal
                fail "insufficient funds"
            bal -= withdraw_amt
    return Account(a.owner, bal)

    OrderState.New -> OrderState.Paid
    OrderState.Paid -> OrderState.Shipped
    OrderState.Shipped -> OrderState.Delivered
    OrderState.Delivered -> OrderState.Delivered
    OrderState.Cancelled -> OrderState.Cancelled
    _ -> state

fn can_transition(from: OrderState, to: OrderState) -> bool = when from
    OrderState.New -> to == OrderState.Paid or to == OrderState.Cancelled
    OrderState.Paid -> to == OrderState.Shipped or to == OrderState.Cancelled
    OrderState.Shipped -> to == OrderState.Delivered
    OrderState.Delivered -> false
    OrderState.Cancelled -> false
    _ -> false

type Account = record(owner: str, balance: dec)

fn apply_transactions(acct: Account, amounts: list<dec>) -> Account
    let mut current = acct
    for amount in amounts
        if amount > 0.0
            current = Account(current.owner, current.balance + amount)
        elif amount < 0.0
            let withdraw_amount = -amount
            if withdraw_amount > current.balance
                fail "insufficient funds"
            current = Account(current.owner, current.balance + amount)
        else
            pass
    return current

Define type Account = record(owner: str, balance: dec, overdraft_limit: dec) and type Transaction = record(is_deposit: bool, amount: dec). If tx.amount is not positive, fail. If tx.is_deposit is true, add tx.amount to balance. Otherwise subtract tx.amount, but fail if it exceeds balance + overdraft_limit.
solution:
type Account = record(owner: str, balance: dec, overdraft_limit: dec)
type Transaction = record(is_deposit: bool, amount: dec)

fn apply_transaction(acct: Account, tx: Transaction) -> Account
    if tx.amount <= 0.0
        fail "transaction amount must be positive"
    if tx.is_deposit
        return Account(acct.owner, acct.balance + tx.amount, acct.overdraft_limit)
    if tx.amount > acct.balance + acct.overdraft_limit
        fail "overdraft limit exceeded"
    return Account(acct.owner, acct.balance - tx.amount, acct.overdraft_limit)

    expect apply_transaction(Account("b", 100.0, 50.0), Transaction(false, 120.0)).balance == -20.0

prompt: Write fn symmetric_difference(a: list<int>, b: list<int>) -> list<int> that returns the distinct integers that appear in exactly one of a or b, first any from a then any from b.
solution:
fn symmetric_difference(a: list<int>, b: list<int>) -> list<int>
    let out: list<int> = []
    for x in a
        if not (has(b, x)) and not (has(out, x))
            push(out, x)
    for x in b
        if not (has(a, x)) and not (has(out, x))
            push(out, x)
    return out
tests:

    expect len(r1) == 4
    expect r1[0] == 1
    expect r1[1] == 2
    expect r1[2] == 4
    expect r1[3] == 5

    let r2 = symmetric_difference([1, 2], [1, 2])
    expect len(r2) == 0

    let r3 = symmetric_difference([], [1, 2])
    expect len(r3) == 2
    expect r3[0] == 1
    expect r3[1] == 2

solution:
type Student = record(name: str, clubs: list<str>)

fn frequent_clubs(students: list<Student>) -> list<str>
    let all: list<str> = []
    for s in students
        let unique_clubs = s.clubs |> group_by(c => c) |> values |> map(g => first(g))
        for c in unique_clubs
            push(all, c)
    return all |> group_by(c => c) |> values |> filter(g => len(g) > 1) |> map(g => first(g)) |> sort
tests:
test "frequent clubs"
    let res = frequent_clubs([Student("a", ["chess", "math"]), Student("b", ["chess", "art"]), Student("c", ["math", "chess"])])
    expect len(res) == 2
    expect first(res) == "chess"
    expect last(res) == "math"
    let res2 = frequent_clubs([Student("d", ["chess", "chess"]), Student("e", ["art"])])
    expect len(res2) == 0
    expect len(frequent_clubs([])) == 0
    expect len(frequent_clubs([Student("f", ["solo"])])) == 0

Write fn deposit(acc: Account, amount: dec) -> Account and fn withdraw(acc: Account, amount: dec) -> Account. deposit adds amount to balance and appends "deposit {amount}" to history. withdraw subtracts amount and appends "withdraw {amount}", but fails with "insufficient funds" if amount > acc.balance or "invalid amount" if amount <= 0.0. Return new accounts with copied history.
solution:
type Account = record(owner: str, balance: dec, history: list<str>)

fn deposit(acc: Account, amount: dec) -> Account
    if amount <= 0.0
        fail "invalid amount"
    let new_history = acc.history |> map(h => h)
    push(new_history, "deposit {amount}")
    return Account(acc.owner, acc.balance + amount, new_history)

fn withdraw(acc: Account, amount: dec) -> Account
    if amount <= 0.0
        fail "invalid amount"
    if amount > acc.balance
        fail "insufficient funds"
    let new_history = acc.history |> map(h => h)
    push(new_history, "withdraw {amount}")
    return Account(acc.owner, acc.balance - amount, new_history)

Write recursive functions `fn find_depth(t: Tree, target: int) -> int` and its helper `fn find_in_children(children: list<Tree>, target: int) -> int` that return the depth (root = 1) of the first node with `value == target`, or 0 if not found.
solution:
type Tree = record(value: int, children: list<Tree>)

fn find_depth(t: Tree, target: int) -> int
    if t.value == target
        return 1
    let d = find_in_children(t.children, target)
    if d == 0
        return 0
    return d + 1

fn find_in_children(children: list<Tree>, target: int) -> int
    if len(children) == 0
        return 0
    let d = find_depth(first(children), target)
    if d > 0
        return d
    return find_in_children(skip(children, 1), target)
tests:

    expect find_depth(Tree(1, [Tree(2, [])]), 2) == 2

    expect find_depth(Tree(1, [Tree(2, [])]), 9) == 0

        return list<int>()
    let cols = len(first(grid))
    let out: list<int> = []
    for c in range(0, cols)
        let mut total = 0
        for row in grid
            total += (row |> skip(c) |> first)
        push(out, total)
    return out

prompt: Write fn transpose(grid: list<list<int>>) -> list<list<int>> that returns the transpose of a rectangular matrix.
solution:
fn transpose(grid: list<list<int>>) -> list<list<int>>
    if len(grid) == 0
        return list<list<int>>()
    let cols = len(first(grid))
    let out: list<list<int>> = []
    for c in range(0, cols)
        let new_row: list<int> = []
        for row in grid
            push(new_row, first(skip(row, c)))
        push(out, new_row)
    return out
tests:

    expect t |> map(row => row |> join(",")) |> join(";") == "1,4;2,5;3,6"
    expect transpose([[1]]) |> map(row => row |> join(",")) |> join(";") == "1"
    expect len(transpose(list<list<int>>())) == 0

prompt: Write fn cell_at(grid: list<list<int>>, row: int, col: int) -> int? that returns the value at the given row and column, or none if the position is out of bounds.
solution:
fn cell_at(grid: list<list<int>>, row: int, col: int) -> int?
    if row < 0 or col < 0 or row >= len(grid)
        return none
    let r = grid |> skip(row) |> first
    if col >= len(r)
        return none
    return r |> skip(col) |> first

    expect cell_at([[1, 2], [3, 4]], 1, 0) == 3
    expect cell_at([[1, 2], [3, 4]], 2, 0) == none
    expect cell_at([[1, 2], [3, 4]], 0, -1) == none

prompt: Write fn diagonal(rows: list<list<int>>) -> list<int> that returns the main diagonal of a square matrix. If the matrix is empty, return an empty list.
solution:
fn diagonal(rows: list<list<int>>) -> list<int>
    if len(rows) == 0
        return list<int>()
    let out: list<int> = []
    let mut i = 0
    while i < len(rows)
        push(out, rows[i][i])
        i += 1
    return out

prompt: Write fn grid_get(rows: list<list<int>>, r: int, c: int, fallback: int) -> int that returns the value at row r and column c in a ragged matrix, or fallback if the row or column is out of bounds.
solution:
fn grid_get(rows: list<list<int>>, r: int, c: int, fallback: int) -> int
    if r < 0 or r >= len(rows)
        return fallback
    let row = rows |> skip(r) |> first
    if c < 0 or c >= len(row)
        return fallback
    return row |> skip(c) |> first

type Time = record(hours: int, minutes: int)

fn add_minutes(t: Time, delta: int) -> Time

    let m = total % 60

prompt: Define type Duration = record(days: int, hours: int, mins: int). Write fn normalize(d: Duration) -> Duration that carries extra minutes into hours and extra hours into days, returning a normalized Duration. For example, Duration(0, 25, 70) should become Duration(1, 2, 10).
solution:
type Duration = record(days: int, hours: int, mins: int)

fn normalize(d: Duration) -> Duration
    let total = d.days * 1440 + d.hours * 60 + d.mins
    let days = total / 1440
    let rem = total % 1440
    let hours = rem / 60
    let mins = rem % 60
    return Duration(days, hours, mins)

    expect normalize(Duration(0, 25, 70)).mins == 10

    expect normalize(Duration(0, 0, 60)).mins == 0
    expect normalize(Duration(1, 0, 0)).days == 1

prompt: Define type Time = record(hours: int, minutes: int) representing a time of day. Write fn time_to_minutes(t: Time) -> int, fn minutes_to_time(total: int) -> Time that wraps into 0..1439 minutes, and fn add_time(t: Time, delta: int) -> Time that adds delta minutes to a time of day and wraps around 24 hours. Assume delta can be negative.
solution:
type Time = record(hours: int, minutes: int)

fn time_to_minutes(t: Time) -> int = t.hours * 60 + t.minutes

fn minutes_to_time(total: int) -> Time
    let normalized = ((total % 1440) + 1440) % 1440
    let h = normalized / 60
    let m = normalized % 60
    return Time(h, m)

fn add_time(t: Time, delta: int) -> Time = minutes_to_time(time_to_minutes(t) + delta)
tests:

    expect time_to_minutes(Time(1, 2)) == 62
    expect minutes_to_time(0).hours == 0
    expect minutes_to_time(0).minutes == 0
    expect minutes_to_time(1439).hours == 23
    expect minutes_to_time(1439).minutes == 59
    expect minutes_to_time(1440).hours == 0
    expect add_time(Time(23, 50), 20).hours == 0
    expect add_time(Time(23, 50), 20).minutes == 10
    expect add_time(Time(0, 10), -20).hours == 23
    expect add_time(Time(0, 10), -20).minutes == 50

prompt: Write fn restock(items: list<Item>, product: str, extra: int) -> list<Item> that returns a new cart where the item named product has its qty increased by extra. If no such item exists, append a new Item(product, 0.0, extra). Define Item as record(name: str, price: dec, qty: int).
solution:
type Item = record(name: str, price: dec, qty: int)

fn restock(items: list<Item>, product: str, extra: int) -> list<Item>
    let out: list<Item> = []
    let mut found = false
    for i in items
        if i.name == product
            push(out, Item(i.name, i.price, i.qty + extra))
            found = true
        else
            push(out, i)
    if not found
        push(out, Item(product, 0.0, extra))
    return out
tests:
test "restock existing"
    let r = restock([Item("tea", 2.5, 3), Item("cake", 4.0, 1)], "tea", 2)
    expect r |> map(i => i.name) |> join(",") == "tea,cake"
    expect r |> sum(i => i.qty) == 6
    expect r |> sum(i => i.price * i.qty) == 16.5

test "restock new"
    let r = restock([Item("tea", 2.5, 3)], "milk", 4)
    expect r |> map(i => i.name) |> join(",") == "tea,milk"
    expect r |> sum(i => i.qty) == 7
    expect r |> sum(i => i.price * i.qty) == 7.5

prompt: Define type Point = record(row: int, col: int). Write fn max_pos(m: list<list<int>>) -> Point? that returns the position of the maximum value in a non-empty matrix, or none if the matrix is empty. If there are ties, return the first one in row-major order.
solution:
type Point = record(row: int, col: int)

fn max_pos(m: list<list<int>>) -> Point?
    if len(m) == 0
        return none
    let cols = len(first(m))
    let mut best: Point? = none
    let mut best_val = 0
    let mut found = false
    for r in range(0, len(m))
        for c in range(0, cols)
            let v = m |> skip(r) |> first |> skip(c) |> first
            if not found or v > best_val
                best = Point(r, c)
                best_val = v
                found = true
    return best
tests:
test "max_pos finds first maximum"
    expect max_pos([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) == Point(1, 1)
    expect max_pos([[5, 5], [1, 2]]) == Point(0, 0)
    let empty: list<list<int>> = []
    expect max_pos(empty) == none

prompt: Write fn at(m: list<list<int>>, r: int, c: int) -> int? and fn sum_around(m: list<list<int>>, r: int, c: int) -> int that returns the sum of the up to four orthogonal neighbors (up, down, left, right) of the cell at row r, column c. Ignore neighbors that are out of bounds. If the center cell is out of bounds, return 0.
solution:
fn at(m: list<list<int>>, r: int, c: int) -> int?
    if r < 0 or r >= len(m)
        return none
    let row = m |> skip(r) |> first
    if c < 0 or c >= len(row)
        return none
    return row |> skip(c) |> first

fn sum_around(m: list<list<int>>, r: int, c: int) -> int
    if at(m, r, c) == none
        return 0
    let mut total = 0
    for dr in [-1, 0, 1]
        for dc in [-1, 0, 1]
            if abs(dr) + abs(dc) == 1
                let v = at(m, r + dr, c + dc)
                if v != none
                    total += v.Value
    return total

type Row = record(label: str, value: int)

fn table_row(r: Row) -> str
    let pad = repeat(" ", max(0, 8 - len(r.label)))
    return "{r.label}{pad} | {r.value}"

fn table(rows: list<Row>) -> str
    let lines = rows |> map(r => table_row(r))
    let body = lines |> join("\n")
    if len(lines) == 0
        return "label    | value"
    else
        return "label    | value\n{body}"

solution:
fn binary_search(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int?
    let mut lo = 0
    let mut hi = len(xs) - 1
    while lo <= hi
        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        let mid_val = xs |> skip(mid) |> first
        if mid_val == target
            return mid
        elif mid_val < target
            lo = mid + 1
        else
            hi = mid - 1
    return none

solution:
fn binary_search(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int?
    let mut low = 0
    let mut high = len(xs) - 1
    while low <= high
        let mid = floor(dec(low + high) / 2.0)
        if xs[mid] == target
            return mid
        elif xs[mid] < target
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid - 1
    return none

prompt: Write fn lower_bound(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int that returns the index of the first element in the sorted list xs that is greater than or equal to target, or len(xs) if no such element exists. Write fn upper_bound(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int that returns the index of the first element that is greater than target, or len(xs). Assume xs is sorted ascending.
solution:
fn lower_bound(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int
    let mut low = 0
    let mut high = len(xs)
    while low < high
        let mid = floor(dec(low + high) / 2.0)
        if xs[mid] < target
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid
    return low

fn upper_bound(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int
    let mut low = 0
    let mut high = len(xs)
    while low < high
        let mid = floor(dec(low + high) / 2.0)
        if xs[mid] <= target
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid
    return low
tests:
test "lower_bound finds first >= target"
    expect lower_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 3) == 1
    expect lower_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 4) == 3
    expect lower_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 0) == 0
    expect lower_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 8) == 5
    expect lower_bound(list<int>(), 2) == 0

test "upper_bound finds first > target"
    expect upper_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 3) == 3
    expect upper_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 4) == 3
    expect upper_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 0) == 0
    expect upper_bound([1, 3, 3, 5, 7], 8) == 5
    expect upper_bound(list<int>(), 2) == 0

prompt: Write fn binary_search(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int that assumes xs is sorted ascending and returns the index of target, or -1 if it is absent. Use binary search.
solution:
fn binary_search(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int
    let mut low = 0
    let mut high = len(xs) - 1
    while low <= high
        let mid = (low + high) / 2
        if xs[mid] == target
            return mid
        elif xs[mid] < target
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid - 1
    return -1

    expect binary_search([1, 3, 5, 7], 4) == -1

solution:
type Book = record(title: str, pages: int)

fn binary_search_book(books: list<Book>, title: str) -> int
    let mut low = 0
    let mut high = len(books)
    while low < high
        let mid = (low + high) / 2
        if books[mid].title.CompareTo(title) < 0
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid
    if low < len(books) and books[low].title == title
        return low
    return -1

fn median(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    let sorted = sort(xs)
    let n = len(sorted)
    if n % 2 == 1
        return sorted |> skip(n / 2) |> first
    let a = sorted |> skip(n / 2 - 1) |> first
    let b = sorted |> skip(n / 2) |> first
    return (a + b) / 2.0

fn median(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    if len(xs) == 0
        return 0.0
    let sorted = sort(xs)
    let mid = len(sorted) / 2
    if len(sorted) == mid * 2 + 1
        return skip(sorted, mid) |> first
    let a = skip(sorted, mid - 1) |> first
    let b = skip(sorted, mid) |> first
    return (a + b) / 2.0

fn binary_search(xs: list<int>, target: int) -> int?
    let mut low = 0
    let mut high = len(xs) - 1
    while low <= high
        let mid = low + (high - low) / 2
        if xs[mid] == target
            return mid
        elif xs[mid] < target
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid - 1
    return none

fn median(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    let sorted = sort(xs)
    let n = len(sorted)
    if n == 0
        return 0.0
    if n % 2 == 1
        return first(skip(sorted, n / 2))
    let a = first(skip(sorted, n / 2 - 1))
    let b = first(skip(sorted, n / 2))
    return (a + b) / 2.0

fn mode(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    if len(xs) == 0
        return 0.0
    let sorted = sort(xs)
    let mut best = first(sorted)
    let mut best_count = 0
    let mut current = first(sorted)
    let mut current_count = 0
    for x in sorted
        if x == current
            current_count = current_count + 1
        else
            if current_count > best_count
                best = current
                best_count = current_count
            current = x
            current_count = 1
    if current_count > best_count
        best = current
        best_count = current_count
    return best

solution:
type Stats = record(avg: dec, median: dec, mode: dec)

fn mean(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    if len(xs) == 0
        return 0.0
    return sum(xs) / dec(len(xs))

fn median(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    let ys = sort(xs)
    let n = len(ys)
    if n == 0
        return 0.0
    elif n % 2 == 1
        return ys |> skip((n - 1) / 2) |> first
    else
        let mid1 = ys |> skip(n / 2 - 1) |> first
        let mid2 = ys |> skip(n / 2) |> first
        return (mid1 + mid2) / 2.0

fn mode(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    if len(xs) == 0
        return 0.0
    let uniq = sort(distinct(xs))
    return uniq |> max_by(x => count(xs, y => y == x))

fn summarize(xs: list<dec>) -> Stats =
    Stats(mean(xs), median(xs), mode(xs))

solution:
fn mode(xs: list<dec>) -> dec
    if len(xs) == 0
        return 0.0
    let sorted = sort(xs)
    let mut best = first(sorted)
    let mut best_count = 0
    let mut current = first(sorted)
    let mut current_count = 0
    for x in sorted
        if x == current
            current_count += 1
        else
            if current_count > best_count
                best = current
                best_count = current_count
            current = x
            current_count = 1
    if current_count > best_count
        best = current
        best_count = current_count
    return best
tests:

    let mut q: list<int> = []
    let out: list<int> = []
    for c in cmds
        if c.op == "enqueue"
            let new_q: list<int> = []
            for e in q

            q = new_q

                push(out, first(q))
                q = skip(q, 1)
    return out

type Customer = record(name: str, service: int)

fn serve_customers(customers: list<Customer>, limit: int) -> list<str>
    let mut q = customers
    let mut remaining = limit
    let served: list<str> = []
    while len(q) > 0
        let c = first(q)
        if c.service <= remaining
            push(served, c.name)
            remaining -= c.service
            q = skip(q, 1)
        else
            return served
    return served

Write fn bowling_total(rolls: list<int>) -> int that scores a full 10-frame bowling game from a flat list of rolls. For each frame, if the first roll is 10, score 10 plus the next two rolls; if the two rolls sum to 10, score 10 plus the next roll; otherwise score the sum of the two rolls. Assume rolls has enough rolls.
solution:
fn bowling_total(rolls: list<int>) -> int
    let mut score = 0
    let mut remaining = rolls
    let mut frame = 0
    while frame < 10
        let first_roll = first(remaining)
        if first_roll == 10
            score += 10 + first(skip(remaining, 1)) + first(skip(remaining, 2))
            remaining = skip(remaining, 1)
        else
            let second_roll = first(skip(remaining, 1))
            if first_roll + second_roll == 10
                score += 10 + first(skip(remaining, 2))
            else
                score += first_roll + second_roll
            remaining = skip(remaining, 2)
        frame += 1
    return score

Write fn dequeue(q: TwoStackQueue) -> int that removes and returns the front element. Write fn peek_queue(q: TwoStackQueue) -> int that returns the front element without removing it. Assume dequeue and peek are not called on an empty queue.
solution:
type TwoStackQueue = record(inbox: list<int>, outbox: list<int>)

fn enqueue(q: TwoStackQueue, x: int)
    push(q.inbox, x)

fn dequeue(q: TwoStackQueue) -> int
    if len(q.outbox) == 0
        while len(q.inbox) > 0
            push(q.outbox, last(q.inbox))
            q.inbox.RemoveAt(len(q.inbox) - 1)
    let x = last(q.outbox)
    q.outbox.RemoveAt(len(q.outbox) - 1)
    return x

fn peek_queue(q: TwoStackQueue) -> int
    if len(q.outbox) == 0
        while len(q.inbox) > 0
            push(q.outbox, last(q.inbox))
            q.inbox.RemoveAt(len(q.inbox) - 1)
    return last(q.outbox)

    enqueue(q, 3)
    expect peek_queue(q) == 1
    expect dequeue(q) == 1
    expect dequeue(q) == 2
    enqueue(q, 4)

solution:
type JobKind = enum(Email, Report)
type Job = record(id: int, kind: JobKind)

fn enqueue_job(q: list<Job>, j: Job)
    push(q, j)

fn process_jobs(q: list<Job>) -> list<Job>
    let out: list<Job> = []
    while len(q) > 0
        push(out, first(q))
        q.RemoveAt(0)
    return out

fn count_kind(q: list<Job>, kind: JobKind) -> int =
    q |> count(j => j.kind == kind)
tests:

    expect count_kind(q, JobKind.Email) == 0

    enqueue_job(q, Job(3, JobKind.Email))
    expect count_kind(q, JobKind.Email) == 2
    expect count_kind(q, JobKind.Report) == 1
    let out = process_jobs(q)
    expect len(out) == 3
    let j1 = first(out)
    expect j1.id == 1
    expect j1.kind == JobKind.Email
    out.RemoveAt(0)
    let j2 = first(out)
    expect j2.id == 2
    expect j2.kind == JobKind.Report
    out.RemoveAt(0)
    let j3 = first(out)
    expect j3.id == 3
    expect j3.kind == JobKind.Email
    out.RemoveAt(0)
    expect len(out) == 0
    expect len(q) == 0

fn sum_numbers(s: str) -> int
    let mut total = 0
    let mut current: list<str> = []
    for ch in chars(s)
        if has("0123456789", to_str(ch))
            push(current, to_str(ch))
        elif len(current) > 0
            total += to_int(join(current, ""))
            current = []
    if len(current) > 0
        total += to_int(join(current, ""))
    return total

    expect sum_numbers("007") == 7

solution:
type TimeSlot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn busy_minutes(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> int
    if len(slots) == 0
        return 0
    let sorted = sort_by(slots, s => s.start)
    let mut cur_start = sorted[0].start
    let mut cur_end = sorted[0].end
    let mut total = 0
    for i in 1..len(sorted)
        if sorted[i].start > cur_end
            total += cur_end - cur_start
            cur_start = sorted[i].start
            cur_end = sorted[i].end
        else
            cur_end = max(cur_end, sorted[i].end)
    total += cur_end - cur_start
    return total
tests:
test "busy minutes"
    expect busy_minutes([TimeSlot(9, 11), TimeSlot(10, 12)]) == 3
    expect busy_minutes([TimeSlot(9, 10), TimeSlot(11, 12)]) == 2
    expect busy_minutes([]) == 0
    expect busy_minutes([TimeSlot(9, 12), TimeSlot(10, 11)]) == 3

fn free_gaps(slots: list<TimeSlot>, day_start: int, day_end: int) -> list<TimeSlot>
    let out: list<TimeSlot> = []
    if len(slots) == 0
        push(out, TimeSlot(day_start, day_end))

    let sorted = sort_by(slots, s => s.start)

    for i in 0..len(sorted)
        let s = sorted[i]
        if s.start > cur_end
            push(out, TimeSlot(cur_end, s.start))
        cur_end = max(cur_end, s.end)
    if cur_end < day_end
        push(out, TimeSlot(cur_end, day_end))
    return out

solution:
type TimeSlot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn free_gaps(slots: list<TimeSlot>, day_start: int, day_end: int) -> list<TimeSlot>
    let out: list<TimeSlot> = []
    if len(slots) == 0
        push(out, TimeSlot(day_start, day_end))
        return out
    let sorted = sort_by(slots, s => s.start)
    let mut cur_end = day_start
    for i in 0..len(sorted)
        let s = sorted[i]
        if s.start > cur_end
            push(out, TimeSlot(cur_end, s.start))
        cur_end = max(cur_end, s.end)
    if cur_end < day_end
        push(out, TimeSlot(cur_end, day_end))
    return out

fn total_free_minutes(slots: list<TimeSlot>, day_start: int, day_end: int) -> int =
    free_gaps(slots, day_start, day_end)
    |> sum(g => g.end - g.start)

solution:
type TimeSlot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn max_overlapping(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> int
    let mut best = 0
    let mut i = 0
    while i < len(slots)
        let t = slots[i].start
        let mut count = 0
        let mut j = 0
        while j < len(slots)
            if slots[j].start <= t and t < slots[j].end
                count += 1
            j += 1
        best = max(best, count)
        i += 1
    return best
tests:
test "max overlapping"
    expect max_overlapping([TimeSlot(9, 11), TimeSlot(10, 12)]) == 2
    expect max_overlapping([TimeSlot(9, 10), TimeSlot(10, 11)]) == 1
    expect max_overlapping([]) == 0
    expect max_overlapping([TimeSlot(9, 12), TimeSlot(10, 11), TimeSlot(11, 13)]) == 2

    return 0

solution:
type TimeSlot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn merge_overlaps(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> list<TimeSlot>
    let out: list<TimeSlot> = []
    if len(slots) == 0
        return out
    let sorted = sort_by(slots, s => s.start)
    let mut cur = first(sorted)
    for s in skip(sorted, 1)
        if s.start <= cur.end
            if s.end > cur.end
                cur = TimeSlot(cur.start, s.end)
        else
            push(out, cur)
            cur = s
    push(out, cur)
    return out

fn free_gaps(slots: list<TimeSlot>, day_start: int, day_end: int) -> list<TimeSlot>
    let busy = merge_overlaps(filter(slots, s => s.end > day_start and s.start < day_end))
    let out: list<TimeSlot> = []
    let mut cur = day_start
    for s in busy
        let start = max(s.start, day_start)
        let end = min(s.end, day_end)
        if start > cur
            push(out, TimeSlot(cur, start))
        cur = max(cur, end)
    if cur < day_end
        push(out, TimeSlot(cur, day_end))
    return out

fn numbers_in(text: str) -> list<int>
    let out: list<int> = []
    let mut current = ""
    for c in chars(text)
        let s = to_str(c)
        if has("0123456789", s)
            current = current + s
        elif len(current) > 0
            push(out, to_int(current))
            current = ""
    if len(current) > 0
        push(out, to_int(current))
    return out

Also define fn merge_slots(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> list<TimeSlot> as needed. Intervals are half-open: a slot starts at start and ends at end, so [start, end).
solution:
type TimeSlot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn merge_slots(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> list<TimeSlot>
    let sorted = sort_by(slots, s => s.start)
    let mut out: list<TimeSlot> = []
    let mut rest = sorted
    while len(rest) > 0
        let s = first(rest)
        if s.start < s.end
            if len(out) == 0
                push(out, s)
            else
                let prev = last(out)
                if s.start <= prev.end
                    let merged = TimeSlot(prev.start, max(prev.end, s.end))
                    out = take(out, len(out) - 1)
                    push(out, merged)
                else
                    push(out, s)
        rest = skip(rest, 1)
    return out

fn free_gaps(busy: list<TimeSlot>, day_start: int, day_end: int) -> list<TimeSlot>
    let merged = merge_slots(busy)
    let gaps: list<TimeSlot> = []
    let mut cursor = day_start
    let mut rest = merged
    while len(rest) > 0
        let s = first(rest)
        if s.end <= day_start
            rest = skip(rest, 1)
        else
            if s.start >= day_end
                rest = skip(rest, len(rest))
            else
                if s.start > cursor
                    push(gaps, TimeSlot(cursor, min(s.start, day_end)))
                cursor = max(cursor, min(s.end, day_end))
                rest = skip(rest, 1)
    if cursor < day_end
        push(gaps, TimeSlot(cursor, day_end))
    return gaps

test "free_gaps"
    let empty: list<TimeSlot> = []
    expect free_gaps(empty, 9, 17) |> map(s => "{s.start}-{s.end}") |> join(",") == "9-17"

prompt: Define TimeSlot = record(start: int, end: int). Write fn union_minutes(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> int that returns the total number of minutes covered by the union of all slots, merging overlaps and touching intervals. Also define fn merge_slots(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> list<TimeSlot> as needed.
solution:
type TimeSlot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn merge_slots(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> list<TimeSlot>
    let sorted = sort_by(slots, s => s.start)
    let mut out: list<TimeSlot> = []
    let mut rest = sorted
    while len(rest) > 0
        let s = first(rest)
        if len(out) == 0
            push(out, s)
        else
            let prev = last(out)
            if s.start <= prev.end
                let merged = TimeSlot(prev.start, max(prev.end, s.end))
                out = take(out, len(out) - 1)
                push(out, merged)
            else
                push(out, s)
        rest = skip(rest, 1)
    return out

fn union_minutes(slots: list<TimeSlot>) -> int =
    merge_slots(slots) |> sum(s => s.end - s.start)

    expect union_minutes([TimeSlot(9, 10), TimeSlot(10, 11)]) == 2

    for s in rest

type Slot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn merge_slots(slots: list<Slot>) -> list<Slot>
    let sorted = sort_by(slots, s => s.start)
    if len(sorted) == 0
        let empty: list<Slot> = []
        return empty
    let out: list<Slot> = []
    let mut cur = first(sorted)
    let rest = skip(sorted, 1)
    for s in rest
        if s.start <= cur.end
            cur = Slot(cur.start, max(cur.end, s.end))
        else
            push(out, cur)
            cur = s
    push(out, cur)
    return out

fn free_slots(busy: list<Slot>, day_start: int, day_end: int) -> list<Slot>
    let merged = merge_slots(busy)
    let out: list<Slot> = []
    let mut cursor = day_start
    for b in merged
        let start = min(max(b.start, day_start), day_end)
        let end = min(max(b.end, day_start), day_end)
        if start > cursor
            push(out, Slot(cursor, start))
        if end > cursor
            cursor = end
    if cursor < day_end
        push(out, Slot(cursor, day_end))
    return out

fn first_fit(busy: list<Slot>, day_start: int, day_end: int, needed: int) -> int
    let gaps = free_slots(busy, day_start, day_end)

prompt: Write fn find_next_free(busy: list<Slot>, day_start: int, day_end: int, duration: int) -> Slot? that returns the earliest free slot of at least duration minutes within [day_start, day_end), or none if none exists. Slot is record(start: int, end: int). You may write a helper free_gaps.
solution:
type Slot = record(start: int, end: int)

fn free_gaps(busy: list<Slot>, day_start: int, day_end: int) -> list<Slot>
    let sorted = busy |> sort_by(s => s.start)
    let gaps: list<Slot> = []
    let mut cursor = day_start
    for s in sorted
        if s.start < day_end and s.end > day_start
            if s.start > cursor
                push(gaps, Slot(cursor, min(s.start, day_end)))
            cursor = max(cursor, min(s.end, day_end))
    if cursor < day_end
        push(gaps, Slot(cursor, day_end))
    return gaps

fn find_next_free(busy: list<Slot>, day_start: int, day_end: int, duration: int) -> Slot?
    let gaps = free_gaps(busy, day_start, day_end)
    for g in gaps
        if g.end - g.start >= duration
            return Slot(g.start, g.start + duration)
    return none
tests:
test "find next free"
    expect find_next_free([Slot(9, 10)], 8, 13, 2) == Slot(10, 12)
    expect find_next_free([Slot(8, 12)], 8, 13, 1) == Slot(12, 13)
    expect find_next_free([Slot(8, 13)], 8, 13, 1) == none
    let empty: list<Slot> = []
    expect find_next_free(empty, 8, 13, 5) == Slot(8, 13)
    expect find_next_free([Slot(14, 15)], 8, 13, 5) == Slot(8, 13)

solution:
type Book = record(title: str, author: str, copies: int)
type AuthorCount = record(author: str, count: int)

fn counts_per_author(books: list<Book>) -> list<AuthorCount> =
    books
    |> group_by(b => b.author)
    |> map(kv => AuthorCount(kv.Key, len(kv.Value)))

fn top_author(books: list<Book>) -> str
    let counts = counts_per_author(books)
    if len(counts) == 0
        return "none"
    let best = counts |> max_by(c => c.count)
    return best.author

type Color = enum(Red, Green, Blue)
type ColoredItem = record(name: str, color: Color, score: int)

type Book = record(title: str, author: str, copies: int)

fn count_by_author(books: list<Book>) -> map<str, int>
    let counts: map<str, int> = map<str, int>()
    for b in books
        counts[b.author] = get(counts, b.author, 0) + 1
    return counts
tests:
test "counts per author"
    let books = [Book("A", "X", 1), Book("B", "Y", 2), Book("C", "X", 3)]
    let counts = count_by_author(books)
    expect get(counts, "X", 0) == 2
    expect get(counts, "Y", 0) == 1
    expect get(counts, "Z", 0) == 0

solution:
fn long_words(s: str, n: int) -> str =

        i += 1
    return none

prompt: Write fn rle_encode(s: str) -> str that run-length encodes s. Each run of the same character becomes the character followed by its count as a decimal integer, e.g. "aaabbc" -> "a3b2c1". Empty string returns empty string.
solution:
fn rle_encode(s: str) -> str
    let cs = chars(s)
    if len(cs) == 0
        return ""
    let mut out = ""
    let mut current = to_str(first(cs))
    let mut count = 1
    for c in skip(cs, 1)
        let t = to_str(c)
        if t == current
            count += 1
        else
            out += current + to_str(count)
            current = t
            count = 1
    out += current + to_str(count)
    return out
tests:
test "rle_encode compresses runs"
    expect rle_encode("aaabbc") == "a3b2c1"
    expect rle_encode("") == ""
    expect rle_encode("a") == "a1"
    expect rle_encode("zzzzzzzzzz") == "z10"

fn rle_runs(s: str) -> list<Run>
    let cs = chars(s)
    let out: list<Run> = []
    if len(cs) == 0
        return out
    let mut current = to_str(first(cs))
    let mut count = 1
    for c in skip(cs, 1)
        let t = to_str(c)
        if t == current
            count += 1
        else
            push(out, Run(current, count))
            current = t
            count = 1
    push(out, Run(current, count))
    return out

    expect first(rle_runs("aaabb")).ch == "a"
    expect first(rle_runs("aaabb")).count == 3
    expect last(rle_runs("aaabb")).ch == "b"
    expect last(rle_runs("aaabb")).count == 2
    expect len(rle_runs("")) == 0

fn decode_rle(s: str) -> str
    let parts: list<str> = []
    let mut prev = ""
    let mut num = 0
    for c in chars(s)
        let cs = to_str(c)
        if has("0123456789", cs)
            num = num * 10 + to_int(cs)
        else
            if prev != ""
                push(parts, repeat(prev, num))
            prev = cs
            num = 0
    if prev != ""
        push(parts, repeat(prev, num))
    return join(parts, "")

solution:
type Run = record(ch: str, count: int)

fn to_runs(s: str) -> list<Run>
    let out: list<Run> = []
    let mut prev = ""
    let mut count = 0
    for c in chars(s)
        let cs = to_str(c)
        if cs == prev
            count += 1
        else
            if prev != ""
                push(out, Run(prev, count))
            prev = cs
            count = 1
    if prev != ""
        push(out, Run(prev, count))
    return out

fn from_runs(runs: list<Run>) -> str
    let parts: list<str> = []
    for r in runs
        push(parts, repeat(r.ch, r.count))
    return join(parts, "")

    expect first(runs).count == 3

    expect last(runs).count == 1
    expect from_runs(runs) == "aaabbc"
    let empty: list<Run> = []
    expect from_runs(empty) == ""

prompt: Write fn caesar(s: str, shift: int) -> str that shifts each lowercase letter in s by shift positions in the alphabet, wrapping around. Non-letter characters are unchanged. For example, caesar("abc", 2) should return "cde".
solution:
fn shift_letter(c: char, n: int) -> char
    let letters = chars("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")
    return when c
        'a' -> first(skip(letters, (0 + n) % 26))
        'b' -> first(skip(letters, (1 + n) % 26))
        'c' -> first(skip(letters, (2 + n) % 26))
        'd' -> first(skip(letters, (3 + n) % 26))
        'e' -> first(skip(letters, (4 + n) % 26))
        'f' -> first(skip(letters, (5 + n) % 26))
        'g' -> first(skip(letters, (6 + n) % 26))
        'h' -> first(skip(letters, (7 + n) % 26))
        'i' -> first(skip(letters, (8 + n) % 26))
        'j' -> first(skip(letters, (9 + n) % 26))
        'k' -> first(skip(letters, (10 + n) % 26))
        'l' -> first(skip(letters, (11 + n) % 26))
        'm' -> first(skip(letters, (12 + n) % 26))
        'n' -> first(skip(letters, (13 + n) % 26))
        'o' -> first(skip(letters, (14 + n) % 26))
        'p' -> first(skip(letters, (15 + n) % 26))
        'q' -> first(skip(letters, (16 + n) % 26))
        'r' -> first(skip(letters, (17 + n) % 26))
        's' -> first(skip(letters, (18 + n) % 26))
        't' -> first(skip(letters, (19 + n) % 26))
        'u' -> first(skip(letters, (20 + n) % 26))
        'v' -> first(skip(letters, (21 + n) % 26))
        'w' -> first(skip(letters, (22 + n) % 26))
        'x' -> first(skip(letters, (23 + n) % 26))
        'y' -> first(skip(letters, (24 + n) % 26))
        'z' -> first(skip(letters, (25 + n) % 26))
        else -> c

fn caesar(s: str, shift: int) -> str
    let n = ((shift % 26) + 26) % 26
    return s |> chars |> map(c => shift_letter(c, n)) |> join("")
tests:
test "caesar lowercase"
    expect caesar("abc", 2) == "cde"
    expect caesar("xyz", 3) == "abc"
    expect caesar("hello", 0) == "hello"
    expect caesar("a b!", 1) == "b c!"

Non-letter characters are unchanged. For example, caesar("abc", 2, Right) should return "cde".
solution:
type Direction = enum(Left, Right)

fn shift_letter(c: char, n: int) -> char
    let letters = chars("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")
    return when c
        'a' -> first(skip(letters, (0 + n) % 26))
        'b' -> first(skip(letters, (1 + n) % 26))
        'c' -> first(skip(letters, (2 + n) % 26))
        'd' -> first(skip(letters, (3 + n) % 26))
        'e' -> first(skip(letters, (4 + n) % 26))
        'f' -> first(skip(letters, (5 + n) % 26))
        'g' -> first(skip(letters, (6 + n) % 26))
        'h' -> first(skip(letters, (7 + n) % 26))
        'i' -> first(skip(letters, (8 + n) % 26))
        'j' -> first(skip(letters, (9 + n) % 26))
        'k' -> first(skip(letters, (10 + n) % 26))
        'l' -> first(skip(letters, (11 + n) % 26))
        'm' -> first(skip(letters, (12 + n) % 26))
        'n' -> first(skip(letters, (13 + n) % 26))
        'o' -> first(skip(letters, (14 + n) % 26))
        'p' -> first(skip(letters, (15 + n) % 26))
        'q' -> first(skip(letters, (16 + n) % 26))
        'r' -> first(skip(letters, (17 + n) % 26))
        's' -> first(skip(letters, (18 + n) % 26))
        't' -> first(skip(letters, (19 + n) % 26))
        'u' -> first(skip(letters, (20 + n) % 26))
        'v' -> first(skip(letters, (21 + n) % 26))
        'w' -> first(skip(letters, (22 + n) % 26))
        'x' -> first(skip(letters, (23 + n) % 26))
        'y' -> first(skip(letters, (24 + n) % 26))
        'z' -> first(skip(letters, (25 + n) % 26))
        else -> c

fn caesar(s: str, shift: int, dir: Direction) -> str
    let n = when dir
        Direction.Left -> ((0 - shift) % 26 + 26) % 26
        Direction.Right -> ((shift % 26) + 26) % 26
        else -> 0
    return s |> chars |> map(c => shift_letter(c, n)) |> join("")
tests:
test "caesar with direction"
    expect caesar("abc", 2, Direction.Right) == "cde"
    expect caesar("cde", 2, Direction.Left) == "abc"
    expect caesar("xyz", 3, Direction.Right) == "abc"
    expect caesar("a b!", 1, Direction.Right) == "b c!"

fn run_length_encode(s: str) -> str
    if len(s) == 0
        return ""
    let out: list<str> = []
    let mut current = first(chars(s))
    let mut count = 1
    for c in skip(chars(s), 1)
        if c == current
            count += 1
        else
            push(out, to_str(current) + to_str(count))
            current = c
            count = 1
    push(out, to_str(current) + to_str(count))
    return join(out, "")

    expect run_length_encode("aaa") == "a3"

fn run_length_decode(s: str) -> str
    let out: list<str> = []
    let mut letter = ""
    let mut digits = ""
    for c in chars(s)
        let ch = to_str(c)
        if has("0123456789", ch)
            digits = digits + ch
        else
            if letter != ""
                push(out, repeat(letter, to_int(digits)))
            letter = ch
            digits = ""
    if letter != ""
        push(out, repeat(letter, to_int(digits)))
    return join(out, "")

    expect run_length_decode("") == ""
    expect run_length_decode("a10b1") == "aaaaaaaaaab"
    expect run_length_decode("z1") == "z"

type Run = record(ch: str, count: int)

fn encode_runs(s: str) -> list<Run>
    let out: list<Run> = []
    if len(s) == 0
        return out
    let mut current = to_str(first(chars(s)))
    let mut count = 1
    for c in skip(chars(s), 1)
        let ch = to_str(c)
        if ch == current
            count += 1
        else
            push(out, Run(current, count))
            current = ch
            count = 1
    push(out, Run(current, count))
    return out

fn decode_runs(runs: list<Run>) -> str
    return runs |> map(r => repeat(r.ch, r.count)) |> join("")
tests:
test "run record encoding"
    expect encode_runs("aaabbc") |> map(r => "{r.ch}{r.count}") |> join(",") == "a3,b2,c1"
    expect decode_runs(encode_runs("aaabbc")) == "aaabbc"
    expect decode_runs([Run("x", 2), Run("y", 1)]) == "xxy"
    let empty: list<Run> = []
    expect decode_runs(empty) == ""

prompt: Write fn caesar_lower(s: str, shift: int) -> str that shifts lowercase ASCII letters in s by shift positions, wrapping around a-z. Other characters stay unchanged. You may define helper functions.
solution:
fn caesar_map(shift: int) -> map<str, str>
    let mut sh = shift
    while sh < 0
        sh += 26
    while sh >= 26
        sh -= 26
    let alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    let m: map<str, str> = map<str, str>()
    for i in 0..len(alphabet)
        let c = alphabet |> chars |> skip(i) |> first |> to_str
        let j = i + sh
        let k = if j >= 26 then j - 26 else j
        let d = alphabet |> chars |> skip(k) |> first |> to_str
        m.Add(c, d)
    return m

fn caesar_lower(s: str, shift: int) -> str
    let m = caesar_map(shift)
    return chars(s) |> map(c => get(m, to_str(c), to_str(c))) |> join("")

    expect caesar_lower("abc", 1) == "bcd"

    expect caesar_lower("ABC", 1) == "ABC"

prompt: Write fn caesar(s: str, shift: int) -> str that shifts both lowercase and uppercase ASCII letters, preserving case, and leaves other characters unchanged. You may define helper functions.

fn caesar_map(shift: int) -> map<str, str>
    let mut sh = shift
    while sh < 0
        sh += 26
    while sh >= 26
        sh -= 26
    let lower = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    let upper = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
    let m: map<str, str> = map<str, str>()
    for i in 0..26
        let c = lower |> chars |> skip(i) |> first |> to_str
        let j = i + sh
        let k = if j >= 26 then j - 26 else j
        let d = lower |> chars |> skip(k) |> first |> to_str
        m.Add(c, d)
        let cu = upper |> chars |> skip(i) |> first |> to_str
        let du = upper |> chars |> skip(k) |> first |> to_str
        m.Add(cu, du)
    return m

fn caesar(s: str, shift: int) -> str
    let m = caesar_map(shift)
    return chars(s) |> map(c => get(m, to_str(c), to_str(c))) |> join("")
tests:

    expect caesar("Hello, World!", 2) == "Jgnnq, Yqtnf!"

    if len(s) == 0
        return ""
    let cs = chars(s)
    let mut out = ""
    let mut prev = first(cs)
    let mut count = 1
    for c in skip(cs, 1)
        if c == prev
            count += 1
        else
            out += to_str(prev) + to_str(count)
            prev = c
            count = 1
    out += to_str(prev) + to_str(count)
    return out

fn rle_decode_simple(s: str) -> str
    let cs = chars(s)
    let mut out = ""
    let mut i = 0
    while i < len(cs)
        let c = cs |> skip(i) |> first |> to_str
        let d = cs |> skip(i + 1) |> first |> to_str
        out += repeat(c, to_int(d))
        i += 2
    return out

prompt: Write fn rle_encode(s: str) -> str that run-length encodes s. Each run of the same character becomes the character followed by its count as a decimal number. For example, "aaabbc" becomes "a3b2c1".
solution:
fn rle_encode(s: str) -> str
    if len(s) == 0
        return ""
    let out: list<str> = []
    let mut current = to_str(first(chars(s)))
    let mut count = 1
    for c in skip(chars(s), 1)
        if to_str(c) == current
            count += 1
        else
            push(out, join([current, to_str(count)], ""))
            current = to_str(c)
            count = 1
    push(out, join([current, to_str(count)], ""))
    return join(out, "")

    expect rle_encode("") == ""

prompt: Define type Mode = enum(Encode, Decode). Write fn caesar(s: str, shift: int, mode: Mode) -> str that shifts every lowercase ASCII letter in s by shift positions. If mode is Encode, shift forward; if mode is Decode, shift backward. Uppercase letters and non-letters are left unchanged.
solution:
type Mode = enum(Encode, Decode)

fn caesar(s: str, shift: int, mode: Mode) -> str
    let alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    let delta = if mode == Mode.Encode then shift else -shift
    return s |> chars |> map(c => if has(alphabet, to_str(c)) then alphabet.Substring((alphabet.IndexOf(c) + delta % 26 + 26) % 26, 1) else to_str(c)) |> join("")
tests:
test "caesar with mode"
    expect caesar("abc", 1, Mode.Encode) == "bcd"
    expect caesar("bcd", 1, Mode.Decode) == "abc"
    expect caesar("xyz", 3, Mode.Encode) == "abc"
    expect caesar("abc", 3, Mode.Decode) == "xyz"
    expect caesar("Hello", 2, Mode.Encode) == "Hgnnq"
    expect caesar("Hgnnq", 2, Mode.Decode) == "Hello"

Write fn ticket_fee(t: Ticket) -> dec that charges base_rate * hours for positive hours (0.0 otherwise), adds 15.0 if lost, and caps the total at 40.0.
solution:
type Vehicle = enum(Car, Motorcycle, Truck)
type Ticket = record(vehicle: Vehicle, hours: int, lost: bool)

fn base_rate(vehicle: Vehicle) -> dec = when vehicle
    Vehicle.Car -> 2.5
    Vehicle.Motorcycle -> 1.5
    Vehicle.Truck -> 4.5
    _ -> 0.0

fn ticket_fee(t: Ticket) -> dec
    let hours_fee = if t.hours <= 0 then 0.0 else base_rate(t.vehicle) * dec(t.hours)
    let with_lost = if t.lost then hours_fee + 15.0 else hours_fee
    return min(40.0, with_lost)

Write fn busiest_doctor(appointments: list<Appointment>) -> str? that returns the name of the doctor with the most appointments, or none if there are no appointments. If there is a tie, return the doctor whose name comes first alphabetically. Write any helper function needed.
solution:
type Patient = record(name: str, age: int)
type Appointment = record(patient: Patient, doctor: str, start: int, seen: int, day: str)
type DoctorCount = record(doctor: str, count: int)

fn doctor_counts(appointments: list<Appointment>) -> list<DoctorCount> =
    appointments |> map(a => a.doctor) |> distinct() |> sort() |> map(d => DoctorCount(d, count(appointments, a => a.doctor == d)))

fn busiest_doctor(appointments: list<Appointment>) -> str?
    if len(appointments) == 0
        return none
    let counts = doctor_counts(appointments) |> sort_by(c => c.doctor)
    let best = counts |> max_by(c => c.count)
    return best.doctor
tests:
test "busiest doctor"
    let appts = [
        Appointment(Patient("Ana", 30), "Dr. Lee", 9, 15, "2024-05-01"),
        Appointment(Patient("Bob", 40), "Dr. Kim", 10, 20, "2024-05-01"),
        Appointment(Patient("Cara", 25), "Dr. Lee", 11, 30, "2024-05-02")
    ]
    expect busiest_doctor(appts) == "Dr. Lee"
    let tie: list<Appointment> = [
        Appointment(Patient("Ana", 30), "Dr. Zoe", 9, 15, "2024-05-01"),
        Appointment(Patient("Bob", 40), "Dr. Adams", 10, 20, "2024-05-01")
    ]
    expect busiest_doctor(tie) == "Dr. Adams"
    let empty: list<Appointment> = []
    expect busiest_doctor(empty) == none

solution:
fn fee_for(hours: int, kind: str) -> dec
    let base = when kind
        "car" -> 3.0
        "motorcycle" -> 2.0
        else -> 5.0
    return when hours
        0 -> 0.0
        < 2 -> base * dec(hours)
        else -> base * dec(hours) * 0.8

    expect fee_for(2, "car") == 4.8

    expect fee_for(2, "truck") == 8.0

type Appointment = record(patient: str, doctor: str, day: int, arrival: int, start: int)

fn waiting(a: Appointment) -> int =
    if a.start > a.arrival then a.start - a.arrival else 0

fn average_waiting(appointments: list<Appointment>) -> dec
    if len(appointments) == 0
        return 0.0
    return dec(sum(appointments, a => waiting(a))) / dec(len(appointments))

fn longest_wait(appointments: list<Appointment>) -> int
    if len(appointments) == 0
        return 0
    return waiting(max_by(appointments, a => waiting(a)))
tests:
test "waiting stats"
    let xs = [
        Appointment("A", "D1", 1, 9, 10),
        Appointment("B", "D2", 1, 9, 12),
        Appointment("C", "D1", 1, 8, 10)
    ]
    expect average_waiting(xs) == 2.0
    expect longest_wait(xs) == 3
    expect average_waiting([]) == 0.0
    expect longest_wait([]) == 0

fn leader(candidates: list<Candidate>) -> str?

solution:
type Spot = record(id: int, floor: int, occupied: bool)
type Ticket = record(hours: int, discount: bool)

fn free_spots(spots: list<Spot>) -> list<Spot> =
    spots |> filter(s => not s.occupied)

fn fee_for(t: Ticket) -> dec
    let base = when t.hours
        0 -> 0.0
        < 2 -> 3.0
        < 5 -> 7.5
        else -> 7.5 + dec(t.hours - 4) * 2.0
    return if t.discount then base * 0.8 else base

fn total_fees(tickets: list<Ticket>) -> dec =
    tickets |> sum(t => fee_for(t))
tests:

    expect len(free_spots([Spot(1, 1, true), Spot(2, 1, false)])) == 1
    expect free_spots([Spot(1, 1, true), Spot(2, 1, false)])[0].id == 2
    expect free_spots([Spot(1, 1, true), Spot(2, 1, false)])[0].occupied == false
    expect len(free_spots([Spot(1, 1, true), Spot(2, 2, true)])) == 0
    expect len(free_spots(list<Spot>())) == 0

test "fees"
    expect fee_for(Ticket(0, false)) == 0.0
    expect fee_for(Ticket(1, false)) == 3.0
    expect fee_for(Ticket(2, false)) == 7.5
    expect fee_for(Ticket(5, false)) == 9.5
    expect fee_for(Ticket(5, true)) == 7.6
    expect total_fees([Ticket(1, false), Ticket(2, false)]) == 10.5

type Outcome = enum(Winner, Tie, NoVotes)

fn top_names(votes: list<str>) -> list<str>
    if len(votes) == 0
        return []
    let names = distinct(votes) |> sort
    let best = names |> map(name => count(votes, v => v == name)) |> max_of
    return names |> filter(name => count(votes, v => v == name) == best)

fn outcome(votes: list<str>) -> Outcome
    if len(votes) == 0
        return Outcome.NoVotes
    let top = top_names(votes)
    if len(top) == 1
        return Outcome.Winner
    return Outcome.Tie

prompt: Write a function `fn has_tie(votes: list<str>) -> bool` that returns true when at least two candidates share the highest vote count. Return false for an empty list.
solution:
fn has_tie(votes: list<str>) -> bool
    if len(votes) == 0
        return false
    let names = votes |> distinct
    let best = names |> max_by(n => count(votes, v => v == n))
    let best_count = count(votes, v => v == best)
    return len(names |> filter(n => count(votes, v => v == n) == best_count)) > 1
tests:

    expect has_tie(["a", "b", "a", "b"]) == true
    expect has_tie(["a", "a", "b"]) == false
    expect has_tie([]) == false
    expect has_tie(["a", "b", "c"]) == true

type Vote = record(candidate: str, district: str)

fn count_votes(votes: list<str>) -> map<str, int>
    let counts: map<str, int> = map<str, int>()
    for v in votes
        counts[v] = get(counts, v, 0) + 1

    let names = votes |> filter(v => v.district == district) |> map(v => v.candidate)

Write fn transfer_count(trip: Trip) -> int counting adjacent stops whose zones differ; empty or single-stop trip has 0 transfers.
solution:
type Stop = record(name: str, zone: int, offset: int)
type Trip = record(stops: list<Stop>)

fn trip_duration(trip: Trip) -> int =
    if len(trip.stops) < 2 then 0 else last(trip.stops).offset - first(trip.stops).offset

fn transfer_count(trip: Trip) -> int
    let mut changes = 0
    let mut prev_zone = 0
    let mut first_stop = true
    for stop in trip.stops
        if not first_stop and stop.zone != prev_zone
            changes += 1
        prev_zone = stop.zone
        first_stop = false
    return changes
tests:

    expect trip_duration(Trip([])) == 0
    expect trip_duration(Trip([Stop("A", 1, 0), Stop("B", 1, 12), Stop("C", 2, 25)])) == 25

Write fn base_fare(zone: int) -> dec (zone 1 = 2.5, zone 2 = 3.0, zone 3 = 4.5, else 6.0) and fn trip_fare(trip: Trip) -> dec. trip_fare sums base_fare for each distinct zone in the trip, then charges full for Adult, half for Child, and 70% for Senior, rounded to 2 decimals. An empty trip costs 0.0.
solution:
type Rider = enum(Adult, Child, Senior)
type Stop = record(name: str, zone: int, offset: int)
type Trip = record(stops: list<Stop>, rider: Rider)

fn base_fare(zone: int) -> dec = when zone
    1 -> 2.5
    2 -> 3.0
    3 -> 4.5
    else -> 6.0

fn trip_fare(trip: Trip) -> dec
    if len(trip.stops) == 0
        return 0.0
    let zones = trip.stops |> map(s => s.zone) |> distinct()
    let total = zones |> sum(z => base_fare(z))
    if trip.rider == Rider.Child
        return round(total * 0.5, 2)
    elif trip.rider == Rider.Senior
        return round(total * 0.7, 2)
    return round(total, 2)
tests:
test "trip fare by zones and rider"
    expect trip_fare(Trip([], Rider.Adult)) == 0.0
    expect trip_fare(Trip([Stop("A", 1, 0), Stop("B", 1, 5)], Rider.Adult)) == 2.5
    expect trip_fare(Trip([Stop("A", 1, 0), Stop("B", 2, 5)], Rider.Child)) == 2.75
    expect trip_fare(Trip([Stop("A", 1, 0), Stop("B", 3, 5)], Rider.Senior)) == 4.9

Write fn merge_ingredients(items: list<Ingredient>) -> list<Ingredient> that combines same name and unit, and fn shopping_list(recipes: list<Recipe>) -> list<Ingredient> that collects all ingredients from all recipes, merges them, and returns the sorted list.
solution:
type Ingredient = record(name: str, qty: dec, unit: str)
type Recipe = record(name: str, ingredients: list<Ingredient>)

fn merge_ingredients(items: list<Ingredient>) -> list<Ingredient>
    let groups = items |> group_by(i => "{i.name}|{i.unit}")
    return groups |> values() |> map(g => Ingredient(first(g).name, (g |> sum(i => i.qty)), first(g).unit)) |> sort_by(i => i.name)

fn shopping_list(recipes: list<Recipe>) -> list<Ingredient>
    let all: list<Ingredient> = []
    for r in recipes
        for i in r.ingredients
            push(all, i)
    return merge_ingredients(all)

prompt: Define type Stop = record(name: str, minutes: int, zone: int) and type Trip = record(line: str, stops: list<Stop>). Write fn trip_time(trip: Trip) -> int that sums minutes from the second stop onward. Write fn highest_zone(trip: Trip) -> int that returns the maximum zone in the trip. Write fn trip_fare(trip: Trip) -> dec that uses fare(zone: int) -> dec (2.0 for 1, 3.5 for 2, 5.0 for 3, else 7.5) and charges the fare for the highest zone.
solution:
type Stop = record(name: str, minutes: int, zone: int)
type Trip = record(line: str, stops: list<Stop>)

fn fare(zone: int) -> dec = when zone
    1 -> 2.0
    2 -> 3.5
    3 -> 5.0
    else -> 7.5

fn trip_time(trip: Trip) -> int =
    trip.stops |> skip(1) |> sum(s => s.minutes)

fn highest_zone(trip: Trip) -> int =
    trip.stops |> map(s => s.zone) |> max_of()

fn trip_fare(trip: Trip) -> dec =
    fare(highest_zone(trip))
tests:
test "trip_time, highest_zone, trip_fare"
    let trip = Trip("1", [Stop("A", 5, 1), Stop("B", 10, 2), Stop("C", 15, 3)])
    expect trip_time(trip) == 25
    expect highest_zone(trip) == 3
    expect trip_fare(trip) == 5.0
    let single = Trip("2", [Stop("X", 7, 2)])
    expect trip_time(single) == 0
    expect highest_zone(single) == 2
    expect trip_fare(single) == 3.5

prompt: Define type Entry = record(name: str, hours: dec, rate: dec). Write fn weekly_pay(entries: list<Entry>, name: str) -> dec that computes weekly pay for the named person. All entries for that person have the same rate. Regular hours up to 40.0 are paid at rate; overtime hours above 40.0 are paid at 1.5 times rate. If the person has no entries, return 0.0.
solution:
type Entry = record(name: str, hours: dec, rate: dec)

fn weekly_pay(entries: list<Entry>, name: str) -> dec
    let person_entries = entries |> filter(e => e.name == name)
    if len(person_entries) == 0
        return 0.0
    let total = person_entries |> sum(e => e.hours)
    let rate = person_entries |> map(e => e.rate) |> first
    return min(total, 40.0) * rate + max(total - 40.0, 0.0) * rate * 1.5
tests:
test "weekly pay"
    expect weekly_pay([Entry("ana", 25.0, 20.0), Entry("bo", 10.0, 15.0), Entry("ana", 20.0, 20.0)], "ana") == 950.0
    expect weekly_pay([Entry("ana", 25.0, 20.0), Entry("bo", 10.0, 15.0), Entry("ana", 20.0, 20.0)], "bo") == 150.0
    expect weekly_pay([Entry("ana", 25.0, 20.0), Entry("bo", 10.0, 15.0), Entry("ana", 20.0, 20.0)], "cy") == 0.0

Write fn shift_pay(shift: Shift, overtime_multiplier: dec) -> dec that pays the first 40.0 hours at shift.rate and hours above 40.0 at shift.rate * overtime_multiplier. Write fn pay_by_person(shifts: list<Shift>, overtime_multiplier: dec) -> map<str, dec> that sums each person's pay.
solution:
type Shift = record(person: str, rate: dec, hours: dec)

fn shift_pay(shift: Shift, overtime_multiplier: dec) -> dec =
    shift.rate * min(shift.hours, 40.0) + shift.rate * overtime_multiplier * max(0.0, shift.hours - 40.0)

fn pay_by_person(shifts: list<Shift>, overtime_multiplier: dec) -> map<str, dec>
    let totals: map<str, dec> = map<str, dec>()
    for s in shifts
        totals[s.person] = get(totals, s.person, 0.0) + shift_pay(s, overtime_multiplier)
    return totals
tests:
test "pay_by_person groups total pay"
    let totals = pay_by_person([Shift("Ana", 20.0, 45.0), Shift("Bo", 15.0, 40.0), Shift("Ana", 10.0, 10.0)], 1.5)
    expect get(totals, "Ana", 0.0) == 1050.0
    expect get(totals, "Bo", 0.0) == 600.0
    expect get(totals, "Cal", 0.0) == 0.0
    expect len(totals) == 2

type Timesheet = record(name: str, hours: list<dec>, rate: dec)
type PayLine = record(name: str, pay: dec)

type Timesheet = record(name: str, hours: dec, rate: dec)

fn pay(t: Timesheet, overtime_after: dec) -> dec
    let regular = min(t.hours, overtime_after) * t.rate

    return regular + extra

Also write fn transfer_count(trips: list<Trip>) -> int that counts transfers: a transfer happens when a trip's from stop is not the previous trip's to stop.
solution:
type Trip = record(from: str, to: str, minutes: int)

fn total_time(trips: list<Trip>) -> int =
    trips |> sum(t => t.minutes)

fn transfer_count(trips: list<Trip>) -> int
    if len(trips) == 0
        return 0
    let mut prev = first(trips).to
    let mut transfers = 0
    for t in skip(trips, 1)
        if t.from != prev
            transfers += 1
        prev = t.to
    return transfers
tests:
test "total_time sums trip minutes"
    expect total_time([Trip("A", "B", 10), Trip("B", "C", 15)]) == 25
    expect total_time(list<Trip>()) == 0
    expect total_time([Trip("A", "B", 7)]) == 7

test "transfer_count"
    let trips = [Trip("A", "B", 10), Trip("B", "C", 15), Trip("X", "Y", 5), Trip("Y", "Z", 5)]
    expect transfer_count(trips) == 1
    expect transfer_count(list<Trip>()) == 0
    expect transfer_count([Trip("A", "B", 1)]) == 0

solution:
fn span(xs: list<int>) -> int
    if len(xs) == 0
        return 0
    let mut lo = first(xs)
    let mut hi = first(xs)
    for x in xs
        lo = min(lo, x)
        hi = max(hi, x)
    return hi - lo

solution:
type Player = record(name: str, score: int)

fn top_score(players: list<Player>) -> int
    if len(players) == 0
        return 0
    let best = max_by(players, p => p.score)
    return best.score

fn average_score(players: list<Player>) -> dec
    if len(players) == 0
        return 0.0
    return dec(sum(players, p => p.score)) / dec(len(players))

fn leaders(players: list<Player>, cutoff: int) -> list<str> =
    players |> filter(p => p.score >= cutoff) |> map(p => p.name)
tests:
test "top_score"
    expect top_score([]) == 0
    expect top_score([Player("a", 3)]) == 3
    expect top_score([Player("a", 3), Player("b", 9), Player("c", 5)]) == 9

test "average_score"
    expect average_score([]) == 0.0
    expect average_score([Player("a", 1)]) == 1.0
    expect average_score([Player("a", 3), Player("b", 5)]) == 4.0

test "leaders"
    expect len(leaders([], 5)) == 0
    expect leaders([Player("a", 3), Player("b", 5)], 5) |> join(",") == "b"
    expect leaders([Player("a", 3), Player("b", 5)], 4) |> join(",") == "b"
    expect leaders([Player("a", 3), Player("b", 5)], 3) |> join(",") == "a,b"

Use a loop to build the result.
solution:
type Item = record(name: str, price: dec, qty: int)

fn restock(items: list<Item>, threshold: int, target: int) -> list<Item>
    let out: list<Item> = []
    for i in items
        if i.qty < threshold
            push(out, Item(i.name, i.price, target))
        else
            push(out, i)
    return out
tests:

    let cart = [Item("tea", 2.5, 1), Item("cake", 4.0, 9), Item("milk", 1.2, 3)]
    let out = restock(cart, 5, 10)
    expect out |> map(i => i.qty) |> join(",") == "10,9,10"
    expect out |> map(i => i.name) |> join(",") == "tea,cake,milk"
    expect out |> sum(i => i.price * i.qty) == 73.0
    expect cart |> map(i => i.qty) |> join(",") == "1,9,3"
    expect restock([], 5, 10) |> len() == 0

prompt: Define record Item(name: str, price: dec, qty: int) and enum Stock with values Out, Low, Ok. Write fn level(qty: int, low: int) -> Stock returning Out when qty is 0, Low when qty is below low, and Ok otherwise; fn low_count(items: list<Item>, low: int) -> int counting the items that are Out or Low; and fn low_names(items: list<Item>, low: int) -> list<str> returning the sorted names of the items with qty below low.
solution:
type Item = record(name: str, price: dec, qty: int)

type Stock = enum(Out, Low, Ok)

fn level(qty: int, low: int) -> Stock
    if qty == 0
        return Stock.Out
    if qty < low
        return Stock.Low
    return Stock.Ok

fn low_count(items: list<Item>, low: int) -> int =
    items |> count(i => not (level(i.qty, low) == Stock.Ok))

fn low_names(items: list<Item>, low: int) -> list<str> =
    items |> filter(i => i.qty < low) |> map(i => i.name) |> sort()
tests:
test "stock levels"
    expect level(0, 5) == Stock.Out
    expect level(3, 5) == Stock.Low
    expect level(5, 5) == Stock.Ok
    expect level(9, 5) == Stock.Ok

test "low stock helpers"
    let cart = [Item("tea", 2.5, 0), Item("cake", 4.0, 2), Item("milk", 1.2, 9)]
    expect low_count(cart, 5) == 2
    expect low_count([], 5) == 0
    expect low_names(cart, 5) |> join(",") == "cake,tea"
    expect low_names(cart, 2) |> join(",") == "tea"

    if n % 15 == 0
